Bodies and Creatures: the normal human

Real adult proportions, head to toe, front, side and back. Every drawing is generated from one set of numbers (the canon), so the pictures, the checklist and the scorer always agree.

A faceless figure-drawing mannequin in a fitted base layer. Construction shows Bridgman's masses (ribcage egg, pelvis bowl), the joints and the plumb line. Muscles is a simplified écorché: the groups that change the silhouette.

Eight rules worth more than the rest

7½Heads tall, for a real adult8 is Loomis's ideal, 8½ to 8¾ is the comic hero. A woman is about 93% of a man's height, at about the same head count.
½The middle is the crotchHalf the height falls at the pubic bone. Head and torso take 4 heads; legs take the rest.
1-2-3Chin, chest, navel, crotchOne head apart each, counting down from the chin: chest line, navel, crotch.
2 : 1½Shoulders and hipsMan: shoulders 2 heads, hips about 1½ (1.15 to 1.4 to 1). Woman: shoulders 1¾, hips 1⅔, nearly equal.
E·W·FElbow, wrist, fingertipsArms hanging: elbow at the waist, wrist at the crotch, fingertips at mid-thigh. Arm span equals height.
KThe knee is halfway downBottom of the kneecap sits halfway between the front hip point and the floor (Richer).
|One plumb lineStanding at rest, ear, shoulder, hip joint and the front of the ankle stack on one vertical. Off it, the figure falls.
⇄Masses tilt against each otherRibcage and pelvis are rigid; the waist bends. When the hips tilt one way the shoulders tilt the other (contrapposto).

Body types

Same skeleton, different covering. Landmark heights barely move between average, skinny and heavy; only widths and depths change. Heroic is the one stylisation: longer legs and a smaller head.

AverageRicher's man (7½ heads) and woman (7.4). Use this unless a character asks for something else.
Heroic8½ heads (man), 8.2 (woman). Shoulders 2⅓ heads on a man, narrow waist, extra length in the legs. Muscle grows, joints and hands stay true.
SkinnyLess on the same frame: joints look big, collarbones, ribs and hip points show. Never shorten the limbs.
HeavyMore soft mass on the same frame. Men carry it on the belly in front; women on hips, thighs and seat. Head, hands, wrists and ankles stay their size.

Kids and elders come in a later installment, as their own ranges.

Our toy style

Abbie's World figures stay anatomically true. We push readability, not anatomy: a figure seen small on a phone needs a slightly bigger head, hands and feet, and clear planes.

Exaggerate

  • Head about 3% bigger: 7¼ heads instead of 7½.
  • Hands and feet 10% bigger, so gestures and steps read.
  • The planes where bone is near the surface: collarbone, elbow, kneecap, shin, ankle, the hip points. On paper models these are the folds.
  • The silhouette turns: shoulder to waist to hip, the calf curve, the S of the spine from the side.
  • Gesture: the tilt of the masses, and weight on one leg.

Keep true

  • Every landmark height, measured against the height of the figure.
  • Limb segment lengths: the elbow, wrist and knee where the canon puts them.
  • Shoulder-to-hip ratios inside the real range for each sex.
  • Bust, waist and hips inside real adult ranges. No anime or fantasy shapes.
  • Where fat goes, by sex. Joints never get fat.

Head and hand

The two places modelers go wrong first. Placement marks only: the head shows where features go, never a face.

Head (Loomis)

  • The face is three equal parts: hairline to brow, brow to nose, nose to chin (Loomis).
  • The eyes sit halfway down the head, not two thirds up; the head is five eyes wide.
  • The space between the eyes is one eye; the nose is about as wide as that space.
  • The mouth is a third of the way from the nose to the chin; its corners line up under the pupils.
  • The ear runs from the brow to the nose, behind the middle of the head in profile; the jaw angle sits under its front edge.
  • Men: heavier brow ridge, wider square jaw, bigger nose. Women: smoother brow, narrower jaw, rounder chin, more upright forehead.

Hand (Bridgman, Richer)

  • The palm and the middle finger are about the same length; the whole hand is about the face, chin to hairline.
  • Each finger bone is about 0.6 to 0.7 of the one before it (Bridgman: segments grow by definite proportions).
  • The knuckles form an arc, highest at the middle finger; the little finger's knuckle sits lowest.
  • The index tip reaches the middle of the middle finger's last segment; the little finger's tip reaches the ring finger's last joint.
  • The thumb's tip reaches the index finger's base knuckle when the hand is relaxed; the thumb dominates the hand (Bridgman).
  • On a woman the hand is narrower and the fingers taper more; the proportions along the fingers are the same.

Our paper bodies, scored

The scorer measured the ten paper bodies the Roman kit dresses. They all come out at 8 heads, so heads look too small for the toy rule. Two misses repeat on every body: the knees sit about a quarter of a head too low (the shins are short), and the fingertips stop about a third of a head too high (the arms are short).

BodyHeadsScoreKneeFingertipsShoulder : hipOther misses

Heroic bodies score low on purpose: they are bulked-up average bodies, not heroic proportions (no longer legs, no smaller head).

The checklist a modeler scores against

  1. Head count7¼ heads for toy average (real 7½, heroic 8½). Measure crown to chin, divide the height.
  2. The middleHalf the height at the crotch, within a sixth of a head.
  3. Torso stackChin, chest line, navel, crotch about one head apart.
  4. ArmsElbow at the waist, wrist at the crotch, fingertips at mid-thigh, arm span equal to height.
  5. KneeHalfway between the front hip point and the floor.
  6. WidthsShoulders, chest, waist and hips within 12% of the canon for the build; shoulder-to-hip ratio in the range for the sex.
  7. Side viewThe S of the spine, chest ahead of the belly (unless heavy), seat behind, calf behind the shin, ear over the ankle.
  8. Bones that showCollarbone, elbow, hip points, kneecap, shin and both ankle bones are hard planes, the inner ankle higher than the outer.
  9. Fat and muscleMass goes where the build and sex put it; joints, hands and head stay their size.
  10. PGBase layer always on: briefs, and a fitted top on women. No nudity in any model, image or prompt.

Checks 1 to 6 are automatic: python tools/bodies/score_body.py body.json scores a paper-body file or a plain list of landmark heights and widths.
